title: Open Eyes
victim: Griffith, commander of the Band of the Hawk
teaser: The royal palace of Midland is celebrating the taking of Doldrey. The mercenaries of the Band of the Hawk have been invited to a ball for the first time, and the nobility eye them sourly. At 01:40 Griffith, commander of the Hawks, was found in the orangery. Not a speck of blood on his white cloak, his face calm, as if he'd fallen asleep. His Behelit lies on his chest, and its eyes are open. The guard has locked the gates. The courtiers blame the mercenaries, and the mercenaries blame the courtiers.

habits.label: Hawk feather on the chest
habits.habit: Wears a hawk feather pinned to their chest
clues: A grey hawk feather lies between the lemon tubs, its pin bent. The culprit wears a hawk feather.
A maid saw someone walk towards the orangery with a feather on their chest that bobbed at every step. The culprit wears a hawk feather.

habits.label: Smells of the stables
habits.habit: Smells of the stables however much they wash
clues: The orangery smells of roses, but by the bench where Griffith lay there's a distinct whiff of horse sweat. The culprit smells of the stables.
There are a few bits of stable straw on the orangery's marble floor, and no guest has been to the stables since morning. The culprit smells of the stables.

habits.label: Powders their face
habits.habit: Powders their face heavily before the ball
clues: The dark leaves of the fig tree by the entrance have white smudges of powder, as if someone brushed them with a cheek. The culprit powders their face.
There's a smudge of powder on the collar of Griffith's white cloak, and he didn't powder his face. The culprit powders their face.

habits.label: Mail under the doublet
habits.habit: Wears mail under their doublet even to a ball
clues: A steel ring of chain mail is caught on the thorns of the rose bush by the body. The culprit wears mail under their doublet.
A footman caught a guest who stumbled at the orangery doors and felt iron under the velvet. The culprit wears mail under their doublet.

habits.label: Never takes off spurs
habits.habit: Walks round the palace in spurs, as if about to mount
clues: Fine paired scratches, like from spurs, run across the marble from the orangery door to the bench. The culprit never takes off their spurs.
The guard at the gallery heard someone walk down the corridor to the orangery with a soft jingle of spurs. The culprit never takes off their spurs.

habits.label: Signet ring
habits.habit: Never takes off a heavy signet ring with the family seal
clues: Griffith's wrist has a fresh bruise with a clear pattern, as if grabbed by a hand wearing a signet ring. The culprit wears a signet ring.
Someone's coat of arms is pressed into the damp soil of the tub by the bench, as if a hand with a signet ring leaned there. The culprit wears a signet ring.

habits.label: Never puts down their goblet
habits.habit: Carries a goblet of wine all through the ball and never sets it down
clues: A trail of red wine drops runs across the floor from the ballroom to the orangery. The culprit never puts down their goblet.
A palace goblet, half drunk, stands under the bench. Nobody takes wine into the orangery, and none is served there. The culprit never puts down their goblet.

habits.label: Tudor accent
habits.habit: Speaks with a noticeable Tudor accent and stresses words wrongly
clues: A footman by the orangery made out a few words said to Griffith in a Tudor accent. The culprit speaks with a Tudor accent.
The guard at the guardhouse was given tonight's password with Tudor stress, and he was surprised at such a guest. The culprit speaks with a Tudor accent.

habits.label: Afraid of the dark
habits.habit: Afraid of the dark and never walks the palace without a candle
clues: Drops of wax have set on the floor every few steps from the gallery to the orangery. The culprit is afraid of the dark.
No light was lit in the orangery, yet a candle stub burned almost to nothing stands by the body. The culprit is afraid of the dark.

habits.label: Fans themselves
habits.habit: Fans themselves with a lace fan all evening
clues: A broken mother-of-pearl blade from a fan lies under the lemon tree. The culprit fans themselves.
A maid saw a silhouette in the orangery doorway fanning itself, though it was cool in there. The culprit fans themselves.

habits.label: Drags their scabbard
habits.habit: Carries a sword too long for them, and the scabbard drags along the floor
clues: A neat furrow runs through the sand of the orangery path, as if the tip of a scabbard was dragged along it. The culprit drags their scabbard.
The guard at the gallery heard metal scraping on marble, and the sound went off towards the orangery. The culprit drags their scabbard.

habits.label: Plays dice
habits.habit: Throws dice for money at every spare moment
clues: A die with one corner filed down lies by the fountain. The culprit plays dice.
A footman heard a dry rattle in the orangery, like dice shaken in a fist, then everything went quiet. The culprit plays dice.

habits.label: Eats raw garlic
habits.habit: Eats raw garlic against every ailment, and you can smell it a mile off
clues: Among the roses in the orangery there's a strong smell of garlic, and it still lingers. The culprit eats raw garlic.
Dry garlic skin lies by the bench, and the kitchen served no garlic for the ball. The culprit eats raw garlic.

habits.label: Walks with a greyhound
clues: The wet soil by the tubs has dog paw prints, long and narrow like a greyhound's. The culprit walks with a greyhound.
Long, coarse, pale dog hair is caught on the hem of Griffith's cloak. The culprit walks with a greyhound.

habits.label: Hard of hearing
habits.habit: Deaf in one ear from the cannon at Doldrey and talks too loudly
clues: A footman heard someone's loud voice from the orangery, while Griffith answered quietly as always. The culprit is hard of hearing.
A guard made out Griffith repeating one sentence twice, the second time noticeably louder. The person he was talking to couldn't hear well. The culprit is hard of hearing.

habits.label: Scatters salt against evil
habits.habit: Superstitious, sprinkles a pinch of salt on every threshold against evil spirits
clues: Salt is scattered across the orangery threshold in a thin line from post to post. The culprit scatters salt against evil.
A ring of salt was poured round the Behelit on Griffith's chest, as if someone feared it. The culprit scatters salt against evil.

strong: Griffith was killed by the fountain, then carried to the bench and laid out as if asleep. There are no drag marks: he was carried in someone's arms. The culprit is physically strong.
The heavy tub with the orange tree was pushed against the orangery door from inside so nobody could come in. Afterwards two footmen could barely shift it. The culprit is physically strong.
quiet: The princess's peacocks sleep under the orangery's glass roof, and they scream at the slightest rustle. That night not one made a sound. The culprit moves silently.
Griffith was standing by the fountain with his back to the exit and didn't even turn round. Someone came up to him without his hearing a thing. The culprit moves silently.
tools: Griffith was killed with a single thrust of a thin stiletto into the base of the skull, under the hair. There's hardly any blood, and no second blow was needed. The culprit is a master of the blade.
The cord of the Behelit round Griffith's neck was cut with a single touch, and the skin under it isn't even scratched. The culprit is a master of the blade.
medic: Griffith's goblet has a sediment of poppy draught: he was drowsy before the blow. The culprit is skilled in physic.
The physician says Griffith died instantly and didn't even cry out: the killer knew exactly where to strike. The culprit is skilled in physic.
keys: After sunset the orangery is locked, and only the gardener and the steward have keys. The door was opened with a key, the lock untouched. The culprit had a key to the palace doors.
The grille from the orangery to the wine cellar hasn't been opened in years, yet tonight its hinges are freshly oiled and the lock undone. The culprit had a key to the palace doors.
safe: Griffith was summoned to the orangery by a note in the princess's handwriting. The princess didn't write it. The culprit can read and write.
In the guest book at the guardhouse one name has been scraped out and another written over it in a neat hand. The culprit can read and write.
sched: The blow fell during the changing of the guard at the gallery, in the five minutes when the corridor is empty. The culprit knows the palace routine.
Griffith left the ballroom as soon as the king retired to his chambers, just as the musicians struck up a long dance. The meeting was set for that moment. The culprit knows the palace routine.
tech: The orangery clock was stopped at 00:50 and later moved forward to confuse the time of death. The culprit understands mechanisms.

The princess's mechanical nightingale in the orangery sang nonstop, though it's wound for a quarter of an hour. Its spring was tightened so it would drown out voices. The culprit understands mechanisms.
cash: The guard who should have been standing by the orangery admitted he went off to the guardhouse for a gold coin. The culprit has money.
Griffith's pocket holds a purse stuffed with Tudor gold, and he never carried money. Someone wanted to make him look like a traitor. The culprit has money.
passages: Behind the vine trellis in the orangery a low door was found leading to an old passage to the chapel. Few people know about it. The culprit knows the palace's secret passages.
The soles that left prints by the fountain were caked in the damp clay of the dungeons, though the palace is marble everywhere. The culprit knows the palace's secret passages.
